newsitem.title: UK: Royal Doulton buys Caithness for 5.5 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Royal Doulton buys Caithness for 5.5 mln stg.

text.p: British fine china maker Royal Doulton Plc said on Tuesday it had agreed to buy Caithness Glass Limited, which designs hand-made coloured glass giftware, for a maximum 5.47 million pounds ($8.50 million).
Royal Doulton said it already had irrevocable undertakings and commitments in respect of 85 percent of the company and Caithness was recommending the offer to shareholders.
Royal Doulton, whose brands include Royal Crown Derby, Minton, Royal Albert and Royal Doulton itself, said the deal should be earnings enhancing for the first full year after acquisition.
Caithness is best known for its individually designed glass paperweights as well as for making the trophy for television quiz show "Mastermind."
The glass designer had pretax profits of 555,000 pounds in 1995 and consolidated net assets of 2.6 million pounds.
At completion of the deal, expected on October 28, Caithness is expected to have net indebtedness of around 1.2 million pounds.
Royal Doulton's glassware products accounted for just under 20 million pounds of its total sales of 242.8 million pounds in the year ending December 31, 1995.

"Caithness...can achieve further expansion through Royal Doulton's international and retail distribution networks and Royal Doulton's financial resources will enable it to expand its manufacturing and visitor facilities to achieve further growth," Stuart Lyons, chief executive of Royal Doulton, said.

Alistair Mair, who will continue in his role as chairman and managing director of Caithness after the deal, said the new ownership would bring "the opportunity for more rapid growth than we could achieve on our own". ($1=.6435 Pound)
